exposure: Three groups: isolated CL+/-P, CL+/-P with mild ultrasonographic anomalies, CL+/-P with severe ultrasonographic anomalies
Groups based on the presence and severity of ultrasonographic anomalies in patients with CL+/-P
cohort: 40 pregnant women diagnosed with cleft lip or/and cleft palate (CL+/-P) in antenatal screening
finding: Patients with CL+/-P and additional ultrasonographic anomalies, particularly severe ones, experienced worse obstetric and neonatal outcomes, including lower Apgar scores and increased NICU admissions.
